metadata.note: The Goodyear brothers' Buffalo and Susquehanna - the lumber and coal system across Potter, Cameron, Elk and Clearfield counties, Pa., with its Addison and Wellsville connections to the Erie and its short-lived 1907-16 extension to Buffalo - and the companies that ran its lines before and after it: the Addison and Pennsylvania (to 1898), the Sinnemahoning Valley (to 1893), the Wellsville, Coudersport and Pine Creek (to 1895), the Wellsville and Buffalo (1915-16), the Baltimore and Ohio (operation from Jan 1932), and the affiliated Potato Creek Railroad. Drawn from research/branches/buffalo_and_susquehanna_railroad.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (researched 2026-10-21). Before this layer the map drew no B&S trackage. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn; most are single proven years ([ANCHOR]) or confirmed-only brackets ([OPEN]), because most branch end dates on this road are not sourced. The last scheduled passenger train left Addison on Nov 19 1949.
metadata.ownership_splits: Rule 4 splits, each sharing identical geometry: Addison - Galeton, Addison and Pennsylvania (1887-1890) -> Buffalo and Susquehanna (1898 Goodyear purchase; drawn 1918-1931) -> Baltimore and Ohio (Jan 1932; 1932-1949). Keating Summit - Costello: Sinnemahoning Valley (1887) -> B&S (1893 consolidation; Keating Summit - Wharton 1895). Wellsville - Hickox: Wellsville, Coudersport and Pine Creek (1893) -> B&S (lease Jan 1 1896; part of Galeton - Wellsville 1907-1912). Buffalo - Wellsville: B&S (1907-1915) -> Wellsville and Buffalo (Dec 15 1915 - Nov 17 1916; operator conflict, see that feature). NOT splits: the B&S Railroad (1893), the B&S Railway's 999-year lease (1907-13), the 1910 receivership and the B&S Railroad Corporation (Dec 31 1913) are one 'Buffalo and Susquehanna' company and colour, as the report recommends; the B&O stock purchase of 1929-31 (the B&S still ran the trains until Jan 1932); the formal 1954 merger into the B&O; the paper 'Addison and Susquehanna Railroad'. Only Addison - Galeton has a confirmed B&O-era passenger year, so no B&O feature is drawn for the other lines.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-10-21 (at creation): nothing drawn for freight-only years. Excluded: the Wellsville, Addison and Galeton Railroad (1956-79, freight only throughout); B&O freight years after passengers ended on every line (Addison - Galeton 1950-55; Galeton - Wellsville, Ansonia, Sinnemahoning - Du Bois, Juneau - Sagamore into the mid-1950s); the Goodyear and Lackawanna Lumber Co. logging railroads, the Medix Run Railroad, the Gurnee mine spur, the Buffalo and Susquehanna Terminal Railroad and the Galeton South Branch & Germania (Fowler: 'passengers?'). The Feb 1952 Official Guide shows every surviving ex-B&S line (Tables 30, 64, 65) freight only.
metadata.horsecar_audit: 2026-10-21 (at creation): none - every constituent was steam from opening; nothing trimmed under Rule 5.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-10-21 (at creation): every label follows Rule 6, '<company>: <terminal> – <terminal>' or a branch name.
not_yet_sourced: OMITTED, no confirmed passenger year: Buffalo and Susquehanna Galeton - Gaines Junction - Ansonia (report block [6]; Fowler section 304 lists the stations with no date letter; the 1896-98 Fall Brook agreement was priced per ton). Part of the 1893 B&S main line, so passengers are likely, but no timetable naming a station was found.

OMITTED, no confirmed passenger year: Buffalo and Susquehanna Galeton - Germania - Cherry Springs - Cross Fork Junction - Hull - Wharton (report block [9]; Fowler's only letter is 'Greco 1906G pass?', passenger doubtful by his own mark). A B&S timetable naming Germania, Cherry Springs, Hull or Hammersley - most likely the Oct 27 1907 B&S timetable or the Mar 5 1899 / Jul 1 1901 tables shown as images on nyrails.org - would allow it to be drawn. The Cross Fork Branch is drawn but therefore appears detached from the rest of the system.

[OPEN] ends: Addison and Pennsylvania Addison - Galeton (1887 start and 1890 end are confirmed years only); B&S Addison - Galeton (1918 start; 1898-1917 unproven); B&S Galeton - Wellsville (1907-1912 confirmed; did trains survive the Buffalo line's Nov 1916 closure or reach the B&O era? best leads: Wellsville Daily Reporter, Potter Enterprise, a 1920s Official Guide); B&S Du Bois - Sagamore (1907-1910 confirmed).

[ANCHOR] single years, end and start dates unknown: Wellsville, Coudersport and Pine Creek 1893; Sinnemahoning Valley 1887; B&S Keating Summit - Wharton 1895 (abandonment filed 1935, Austin - Wharton removed 1942); B&S Wharton - Driftwood 1907 and Driftwood - Du Bois 1907 (Du Bois station closed c.1933); B&S Cross Fork Branch 1913 (end year; start unknown); Potato Creek 1919 (rests on reading Fowler's undefined 'GG' as a passenger guide).
Whether any B&S line other than Addison - Galeton carried B&O passenger trains after Jan 1932 is unknown; STEAM's 'passenger service continued' is not route-specific.

Wellsville and Buffalo operator conflict (1915-16): WIKI says the W&B ran the line and reported its own passenger train movements, but WIKI and STEAM also describe a lease back to the B&S Corporation. Drawn as a W&B feature at low confidence; merge into the B&S feature if the lease-back is confirmed.
Buffalo terminal approach: Erie from Feb 4 1907 (WIKI, AMR) vs New York Central / Lake Shore to Exchange Street (Fowler NY 231); drawn over the NYC, switch date unknown.
Every headway_min and avg_speed_kmh in this layer is an estimate; no B&S timetable with times was read.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap: 44.3 mi against the documented 45.9 mi (97%). 100% of the routed length runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O (note: B&S) apart from 0.2 mi of untagged track, and every waypoint (Addison, Elkland, Knoxville, Westfield, Sabinsville, Gaines, Gaines Junction, Galeton) is within 0.7 km of the line. No straight-line leg longer than 300 m. The trace stops at the town centres, which accounts for the ~1.6 mi shortfall against Fowler's 45.9 mi (Feb 1952 Guide Table 30: 45.8). LATER ALIGNMENT: this A&P-era feature (1887-1890) is drawn on the post-1898 route via the Gaines Junction connector; the original line ran Gaines - Galeton direct (about 4.5 mi, abandoned 1898 - WIKI), which is not mapped in OSM. The A&P was also 3 ft gauge until 1895; any realignment at standard-gauging is not known.

segments.note: The Platt-controlled narrow-gauge (3 ft) Addison & Northern Pennsylvania / Addison and Pennsylvania Railway, Addison, N.Y. (Erie connection) - Elkland - Knoxville - Westfield - Sabinsville - Gaines - Galeton; begun at Addison 1882, at Galeton by 1885 (WIKI). Standard-gauged 1895; bought by the Goodyears in 1898 and passed to the Buffalo and Susquehanna (see the B&S feature). Drawn 1887-1890 only: Fowler's letters show stations listed in the 1887 Official Guide ('Summit 1887G') and the 1890 Guide ('Gurnee (Mine Branch) 1890G'). [OPEN] 1887 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service very probably began earlier, but no earlier year is proven. Do not extend without evidence. [OPEN] 1890 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source consulted dates when passenger service on this line actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Service very probably ran c.1885-1898, but those years are unproven. headway_min is an estimate (a branch-line service of about 2 trains each way a day) and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler PA section 301 letters 1887G and 1890G (Official Guide listings) for the two years drawn; WIKI for construction and the 1898 sale. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.

segments.note: Buffalo and Susquehanna era (the Goodyears bought the line in 1898; the NY portion was held by the paper 'Addison and Susquehanna Railroad', but the B&S ran the trains - WIKI). Starts 1918 because the first dated passenger event on this line in the B&S era is the spring 1918 wreck of a B&S passenger train headed to Addison, which slid into the Cowanesque River near Knoxville (WIKI). [OPEN] 1918 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service very probably began earlier, but no earlier year is proven. Do not extend without evidence. Service very probably ran from 1898, but 1898-1917 is unproven. Ends 1931 because the Baltimore and Ohio took over operation in January 1932 (B&O stock control from 1929-31 is not the split - the B&S still ran the trains); WIKI and STEAM say passenger service continued across the change, see the B&O feature. headway_min is an estimate (a branch-line service of about 2 trains each way a day) and is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Baltimore and Ohio operation from January 1932 (WIKI). Passenger service ended on November 19 1949, with the loss of the Railway Post Office: 'Passenger service officially ended on November 19, 1949' (WIKI); 'November 19, 1949 - Last scheduled passenger train leaves Addison' (ALLEG); the last run was 2-8-0 No. 3132 with a coach and combine, the ex-B&S Atlantics having been scrapped in 1947 (STEAM). The Feb 1952 Official Guide still prints Table 30 'Addison and Galeton', but its station index daggers Addison and Sabinsville as freight only, consistent with the 1949 end. Freight continued under the B&O to 1955/56 and then as the freight-only Wellsville, Addison and Galeton (1956-79, Elkland - Addison abandoned 1960) - context only, not drawn. headway_min is an estimate (a branch-line service of about 2 trains each way a day) and is NOT sourced.
sources: Segment-level: WIKI (Jan 1932 takeover; Nov 19 1949 end); ALLEG and STEAM (Nov 19 1949 last train); Feb 1952 Official Guide index daggers (freight only by 1951). The three end-date sources agree but are not independent. Headway and avg_speed_kmh are NOT sourced.

segments.note: Galeton - Kilbourne - Brookland - Newfield Junction (Coudersport and Port Allegany crossing) - Genesee - Hickox - Wellsville, N.Y. (Erie connection), built 1895-96 (WIKI; 'opened in late 1895', ALLEG); the Wellsville - Hickox end was the leased Wellsville, Coudersport and Pine Creek (from Jan 1 1896). Through Buffalo - Galeton trains with a buffet-parlor car ran over it c.1907-1916 (WIKI, AMR). Drawn 1907-1912: Fowler's NY section 205 letters Stanards, Mapes and Shongo 'a' = the 1907 B&S public timetable, and nyrails.org reproduces a Dec 5 1912 B&S timetable listing Wellsville - Galeton with mileages. [OPEN] 1907 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service very probably began earlier, but no earlier year is proven. Do not extend without evidence. [OPEN] 1912 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source consulted dates when passenger service on this line actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Whether passenger trains survived the Buffalo line's closure in Nov 1916, or reached the B&O era, is unknown - the 1949 last train is dated at Addison, not here. The Feb 1952 Guide's Table 65 'Galeton and Wellsville' is headed 'Freight Service only'. headway_min is an estimate (a branch-line service of about 2 trains each way a day) and is NOT sourced.
